The horizontal scale factor is derived by integer division, so noncanonical sampling ratios collapse to discrete resampling cases.
Any ratio outside the small set of special cases falls into the generic resampler rather than being rejected.
The generic resampler writes expanded pixels using the attacker-derived factor; with inconsistent component geometry this can overrun the intended row boundary and trigger memory corruption.
